**Proof.**

Let $A$ be a full-rank linear transformation. We interpret "full-rank" as $A$ being injective (in particular, the square invertible case is included), so that $A^{T}A$ is positive definite and its smallest eigenvalue
$$\lambda_{\min}:=\lambda_{\min}(A^{T}A)>0$$
is strictly positive. (For a square invertible $A$, $\lambda_{\min}=\sigma_{\min}(A)^{2}$.)

Recall that $g$ is $m$-strongly convex, i.e. for all $u,v$ in its domain and all $t\in[0,1]$,
$$g(tu+(1-t)v)\le t\,g(u)+(1-t)\,g(v)-\tfrac12\,m\,t(1-t)\,\|u-v\|_{2}^{2}.$$

We must show that $f=g\circ A$ is strongly convex, i.e. that there exists $\mu>0$ such that for all $x,y$ and all $t\in[0,1]$,
$$f(tx+(1-t)y)\le t\,f(x)+(1-t)\,f(y)-\tfrac12\,\mu\,t(1-t)\,\|x-y\|_{2}^{2}.$$

Fix $x,y$ and $t\in[0,1]$. Since $A$ is linear,
$$A\bigl(tx+(1-t)y\bigr)=t\,Ax+(1-t)\,Ay.$$
Applying the strong convexity of $g$ with $u=Ax$ and $v=Ay$ gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
f\bigl(tx+(1-t)y\bigr)
&=g\bigl(A(tx+(1-t)y)\bigr)\\
&=g\bigl(tAx+(1-t)Ay\bigr)\\
&\le t\,g(Ax)+(1-t)\,g(Ay)-\tfrac12\,m\,t(1-t)\,\|Ax-Ay\|_{2}^{2}\\
&=t\,f(x)+(1-t)\,f(y)-\tfrac12\,m\,t(1-t)\,\|A(x-y)\|_{2}^{2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

It remains to relate $\|A(x-y)\|_{2}^{2}$ to $\|x-y\|_{2}^{2}$. Writing $z=x-y$,
$$\|Az\|_{2}^{2}=z^{T}A^{T}Az\ge \lambda_{\min}(A^{T}A)\,\|z\|_{2}^{2}=\lambda_{\min}\,\|x-y\|_{2}^{2}.$$

Substituting,
$$f\bigl(tx+(1-t)y\bigr)\le t\,f(x)+(1-t)\,f(y)-\tfrac12\,\bigl(m\,\lambda_{\min}\bigr)\,t(1-t)\,\|x-y\|_{2}^{2}.$$

Since $m>0$ and $\lambda_{\min}=\lambda_{\min}(A^{T}A)>0$ (by full rank / injectivity of $A$), the constant
$$\mu:=m\,\lambda_{\min}(A^{T}A)>0$$
is strictly positive. Therefore $f$ is $\mu$-strongly convex.

**Remark on the necessity of full rank.** The argument hinges on $\lambda_{\min}(A^{T}A)>0$, which is exactly the injectivity of $A$. If $A$ were not full rank (had a nontrivial kernel), then for some $z\ne 0$ we would have $Az=0$, and along the line $x=y+z$ the composition $f$ would be affine, destroying strong convexity. Thus the full-rank hypothesis is precisely what is needed.

**Conclusion.** Yes, $f=g\circ A$ is strongly convex; specifically it is $m\,\lambda_{\min}(A^{T}A)$-strongly convex.

### PROOF COMPLETE
